== Biography ==

The Woggle-Bug is an insect of extraordinary size, appearing before the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and their companions dressed as a dandy: a dark-blue swallowtail coat with yellow lining, a white duck vest, fawn-colored knickerbockers with gilt buckles, and a tall silk hat. Standing as tall as the Tin Woodman, he is remarked to be larger than any bug ever seen in the Land of Oz. He takes evident pride in his own strangeness, declaring that surprising people affords him pleasure and that he is entitled to curiosity and admiration rather than being classed with ordinary insects.

According to his own account, the Woggle-Bug spent about three years hidden near the hearth of a country school-house, secretly listening to the lectures of Professor Nowitall, and credits this period with the vast learning he claims for himself, styling himself "T.E.", Thoroughly Educated. He travels afterward with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, offering frequent, often unwelcome, remarks on puns and education along the way. He is present through the group's confrontation with General Jinjur in the Emerald City, the escape from the palace roof, the building of the flying Thing from two sofas and a Gump's head, and the journey south, during which he complains of sea-sickness and survives an attack by Jackdaws that scatters the Scarecrow's straw stuffing, afterward helping see the Scarecrow refilled with money recovered from the Jackdaws' nest.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Nick Chopper]]''' — friend. The Tin Woodman tolerates the Woggle-Bug's abrupt arrival and lengthy self-introduction ("You may say what you please," he tells him briefly), and the two seem bound afterward through shared adventures, from building the flying Thing together to fending off the Jackdaw attack.

'''[[The Scarecrow]]''' — friend. The Scarecrow greets the Woggle-Bug's sudden appearance with startled courtesy ("your abrupt appearance has caused me surprise"), and later praises one of his remarks as "Spoken like a philosopher!", suggesting an easy companionship between them.

'''[[Tip]]''' — acquaintance. Tip grows visibly provoked by the Woggle-Bug's insistence on puns, telling him "your joke is a poor one, and as old as it is poor," yet still crawls free to assist the Woggle-Bug after the Jackdaws' assault, hinting at a wary but loyal bond.

'''[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]''' — acquaintance. Stranded on the mountain, the Woggle-Bug laments "This is a worse prison than the palace," echoed by Jack Pumpkinhead's own fear that "the mountain air isn't good for pumpkins," suggesting shared unease between them in moments of danger.

'''[[General Jinjur]]''' — enemy. When the Woggle-Bug suggests she marry the Queen to settle her rebellion, Jinjur "glared at the insect fiercely," indicating open hostility between them.
